name: Left Ventricular Non-Compaction Cardiomyopathy

criteria.description: Ratio of non-compacted to compacted myocardium > 2:1 at end-systole on echocardiography
Presence of deep intertrabecular recesses perfused from the ventricular cavity demonstrated by color Doppler
Prominent trabeculations predominantly in the apical and mid-ventricular segments of the left ventricle
Exclusion of other causes of cardiomyopathy such as hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (trabeculation ratio >2:1, deep intertrabecular recesses on Doppler, and prominent trabeculations in typical LV segments) must be met
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Cardiac MRI criteria (Petersen criteria) may also be used for diagnosis

pathognomonic.notes: Identified on imaging as hallmark feature

pathognomonic.symptomName: Deep intertrabecular recesses with blood flow
searchTerms: deep heart muscle recesses with blood flow

common.notes: May occur due to ischemia or arrhythmias

occasional.notes: Due to stagnant blood flow in recesses

laboratory: Elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
Possible elevated troponin in myocardial injury
imaging: Echocardiography showing non-compacted to compacted myocardium ratio >2:1
Color Doppler demonstrating deep intertrabecular recesses with blood flow
Cardiac MRI confirming trabecular morphology and extent
genetic: Mutations in sarcomeric genes such as MYH7, ACTC1, and others
Familial inheritance patterns observed in some cases
other: Electrocardiogram abnormalities including arrhythmias and conduction defects
Holter monitoring may reveal ventricular arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of prominent trabeculations and deep recesses
More uniform ventricular dilation without hypertrabeculation
Asymmetric septal hypertrophy rather than trabecular prominence
No deep intertrabecular recesses with blood flow
Diffuse endocardial thickening rather than trabecular non-compaction
Usually presents in infancy with heart failure

redFlags: Sudden cardiac arrest or unexplained syncope
Progressive heart failure symptoms refractory to treatment
references: Jenni R, Oechslin E, Schneider J, Attenhofer Jost C, Kaufmann PA. Echocardiographic and pathoanatomical characteristics of isolated left ventricular non-compaction: a step towards classification as a distinct cardiomyopathy. Heart. 2001;86(6):666-671.

Kohli SK, Pantazis A, Shah JS, et al. Diagnosis of left-ventricular non-compaction in patients with left ventricular systolic dysfunction: time for a reappraisal of diagnostic criteria? Eur Heart J. 2008;29(1):89-95.
Towbin JA, Lorts A, Jefferies JL. Left ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy. Lancet. 2015;386(9995):813-825.
